clue.text: Official to arrange time near hills for appliances

indicators.note: near says the next item stands right beside what came before, so it follows on

parts.note: short for referee, the official in a match
to rig is to arrange or fix something dishonestly
an era is a period of time
tors are rocky hills

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat is told to schedule some time near the hills to deal with household machines.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, common on Dartmoor in England; a referee is the official.
explanation.definitionFit: Refrigerators are kitchen machines that keep food cold, a standard example of household appliances.

clue.text: Swift attack capturing pawn

indicators.note: to capture something is to take it and hold it within

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A chess move: a quick assault that takes a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift attack' reads as one phrase, but 'Swift' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means very fast, a plain synonym of the adjective swift.

clue.text: Unyielding last word, start of terror in the heavens

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: firm means not giving way
amen is said at the very end of a prayer
the first letter of terror

explanation.surface: An apocalyptic scene: a defiant final word, then the beginning of terror in the skies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is an old, poetic word for the sky, the vault of heaven.

clue.text: Foolish despot, in the ear

parts.note: Idi Amin was the brutal dictator of Uganda in the 1970s
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A tyrant described as a fool, said into someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the ear' looks like a homophone signal, but it is defined by the medical word for 'of the ear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means extremely stupid, a straightforward synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Love taupe blend

indicators.note: to blend is to mix things together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A paint-chart or fashion remark: a fondness for a brownish-grey mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' as a verb: to eat something up is to relish it, as an audience eats up a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up praise or attention is to enjoy it greedily, an idiom for loving it.

clue.text: Mythical bird, originally living in a mountain range with amateur veterinarian?

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the range that follows

parts.note: the first part of the South American range, which wraps around the rest
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so just the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of living
the end of the range's name

explanation.surface: A fantasy creature, once at home in the mountains, with a part-time animal doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: ROC plus L sits inside ANDES. In the fable, Androcles pulled a thorn from a lion's paw, and the lion later spared him in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: Androcles treated an injured lion without any training, so he is jokingly an untrained animal doctor.

clue.text: Made with no artificial chemicals and, curiously, no cigar

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters come out oddly arranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A product label boasting it is chemical-free and, oddly, has no cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no cigar' nods to the phrase 'close but no cigar', but its letters are what count.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without synthetic fertilisers or pesticides, hence free of artificial chemicals.

clue.text: Hedgehog is very pleasant, almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so kind'
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Someone gushing that a hedgehog is just about lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: SO NICE loses its last letter. Sonic the Hedgehog is Sega's blue video-game character.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is the famous blue hedgehog of Sega's video games, so a hedgehog by name.

clue.text: Converted Eritrean money to pay a lawyer

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: African currency exchanged to cover legal fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' with 'money' suggests currency exchange, but it signals rearranging the word Eritrean.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is an advance fee paid to secure a lawyer's services.

clue.text: Kept on rethinking dire steps

indicators.note: rethinking something means working it out again in a new form, so the letters get reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone kept going despite having second thoughts about some drastic measures.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue doggedly, which is what 'kept on' means as a verb in the past tense.

clue.text: Spirit I injected into part of DNA

indicators.note: something injected into another thing ends up inside it

parts.note: a gene is a stretch of DNA
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note from a genetics lab: some essence has been inserted into a DNA sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' could suggest alcohol in a lab, but here it is the magical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a magical being of Arabian folklore, so a kind of spirit.

clue.text: It's silly to swallow red beer

indicators.note: whatever is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: daft means silly; the 'It's' just makes the surface a sentence
R is a standard abbreviation for red

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it's daft to knock back a red ale.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside DAFT, after the D. 'It's silly' reads as a whole remark, but it only gives a word meaning silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Draft (British draught) beer is beer drawn from a cask or keg rather than bottled.

clue.text: US agents tracking hacked iPhone in ancient land

indicators.note: a hacked device has been broken into and messed about, so its letters are scrambled
agents tracking something follow behind it, so they come after it

parts.note: the letters of iPhone rearranged
the Central Intelligence Agency, America's spy service

explanation.surface: American spies follow a compromised phone to somewhere in antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was a seafaring civilisation of the eastern Mediterranean coast in antiquity, roughly modern Lebanon.

clue.text: Passage from casual Zen novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary extract taken from a laid-back Buddhist novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' and 'novel' together suggest a quotation from a book; the passage is a waterway and 'novel' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suez Canal is the waterway in Egypt giving ships a route between the Mediterranean and Red Sea.

clue.text: Al Capone's neckwear: first-rate

parts.note: a scarf is worn round the neck
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict: the gangster's scarf or tie is top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's turns the definition into 'Al Capone is', so it leads into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of the Chicago gangster Al Capone, from scars on his cheek.

clue.text: TV and radio made wines free

indicators.note: set free, the letters can wander into any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Broadcasters handed out complimentary bottles of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Television and radio are the broadcast outlets that, with the press, make up the journalism industry.

clue.text: Round container, extremely open

parts.note: a can is a metal container

indicators.note: at the extremes means taking only the first and last letters

parts.note: the two end letters of open

explanation.surface: A description of a circular vessel that is wide open at its ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round container' reads as one phrase, a bowl perhaps, but 'Round' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a musical round, a piece where voices enter one after another with the same melody.

clue.text: Trash, if not porn, for arts museum or opera company

definitions.text: for arts museum or opera company

indicators.note: to trash something is to wreck it, so its letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A culture-war line: rubbish, if not outright smut, suits a gallery or opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trash' reads as a noun for rubbish, but it is a verb telling you to wreck the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: American arts museums and opera companies are typically organised as charitable bodies that do not distribute profits.

clue.text: Change in real time!

indicators.note: to change something is to make it different, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something shifting live, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' does double duty: it is both the definition and the instruction to rearrange REAL plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify it, a direct synonym of change as a verb.

clue.text: Scanners and rulers switching sides at first

indicators.note: switching sides means left becomes right, done to the opening letter only

parts.note: leaders are those who rule; its opening L stands for left

explanation.surface: Security scanners and monarchs trading places at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) at the front of LEADERS is swapped for R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Readers are people who scan text, and also devices such as barcode readers that scan.

clue.text: You and I facing more severe European, perhaps

indicators.note: one thing facing another stands right up against it, so the two are set side by side

parts.note: you and I together are we
sterner is the comparative of stern, meaning severe

explanation.surface: The two of us confront a harsher continental type.
explanation.definitionFit: A westerner is someone from the West, and a European is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Easter game, for example, with muscle car on Saturday and Sunday

indicators.note: on means placed after, so what follows is attached at the end

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
the Pontiac GTO is a classic American muscle car
the abbreviation for Saturday
the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: Weekend Easter plans: games, perhaps, plus a hot rod on Saturday and Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' looks attached to the game, but it gives EG; a muscle car is a powerful American performance car.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg toss is a game where partners throw an egg back and forth, popular at Easter.

clue.text: Prepared, like, half an octopus in the sound?

indicators.note: in the sound means as heard when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: an octopus has eight arms, so half of one has four; 'like' says the creature resembles that

explanation.surface: A chatty, slang-laden remark about something resembling half an octopus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as filler slang but means 'resembling'. The proverb 'forewarned is forearmed' shows the sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Forearmed means equipped in advance for trouble, so ready or prepared.

clue.text: Republican male destroyed kingdom

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: R abbreviates Republican
the letters of male rearranged

explanation.surface: A political headline: a Republican man brought down a monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Narcs reduce marijuana's active ingredient in the end

indicators.note: to reduce something is to cut it down, so its last letter goes

parts.note: the US Drug Enforcement Administration, whose agents are narcs
THC, tetrahydrocannabinol, is the psychoactive compound in cannabis

explanation.surface: Drug agents cut the potency of seized cannabis in the long run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduce' reads as cutting potency but means cut the abbreviation short. A narc is US slang for a narcotics officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is the end of life; 'the end' is a common euphemism for it.

clue.text: Measure around the middle, right? Wrong

indicators.note: wrong means not in the proper state, so the preceding letters are out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone checks a waist measurement and is told they've got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right? Wrong' reads as a contradiction; 'Wrong' is the instruction applied to the word right.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the distance round something, especially round a person's waist or a tree trunk.

clue.text: "Odyssey! A Homeric Retrospective" captivates the president

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the letters are read from right to left
to captivate is to hold captive, so the title holds the answer within it

parts.note: read backwards, the letters 'sey! A H' run through these words

explanation.surface: A title for an exhibition on Homer's epic that enthrals the US leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' sits inside the quoted title as part of an exhibition name, but it is the signal to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutherford B. Hayes was the 19th President of the United States, so one president by name.

clue.text: Rage is the source of confidence level

indicators.note: a word's source is where it begins, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of confidence
to raze a building is to level it to the ground

explanation.surface: A psychological claim that anger is what gives a person self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rage' tempts as anger, but here it is the other sense: 'all the rage', a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a short-lived fashion, the sense of rage in 'all the rage'.

clue.text: Bore unique biting female insect

parts.note: a drag is a tedious thing or person, a bore

indicators.note: something biting holds its prey between its jaws, so it goes around it

parts.note: an only child is unique in having no siblings
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A dull, one-of-a-kind female bug that bites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting female insect' looks like a description of a mosquito; the definition is just 'insect', and 'biting' tells you to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonfly is a long-bodied predatory insect with two pairs of clear wings.
